introduction: The Parliament has the power to amend the Constitution under Article 368. Among over 100 amendments, the 42nd, 44th, 73rd, and 74th are the most significant because they fundamentally changed the democratic, social, and administrative landscape of India.

core_concepts.title: 42nd Amendment Act (1976)
core_concepts.description: Known as the 'Mini-Constitution' because of its massive scope. It added three new words to the Preamble: Socialist, Secular, and Integrity. It also introduced Fundamental Duties (Part IVA) for citizens.

core_concepts.title: 44th Amendment Act (1978)
core_concepts.description: Enacted primarily to undo the 'excesses' of the 42nd Amendment. Its most famous move was removing the 'Right to Property' from the list of Fundamental Rights.

core_concepts.title: 73rd Amendment Act (1992)
core_concepts.description: Granted constitutional status to 'Panchayati Raj Institutions' (Rural Local Government). It fulfilled the dream of grassroot democracy.

core_concepts.title: 74th Amendment Act (1992)
core_concepts.description: Granted constitutional status to 'Municipalities' (Urban Local Bodies), ensuring uniform governance in cities and towns.

important_entities.name: Indira Gandhi vs. Morarji Desai
important_entities.significance: The 42nd was passed by Indira Gandhi during the Emergency. The 44th was passed by the Morarji Desai (Janata Party) government to restore democratic balances.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.alert_title: Right to Property is NOT gone
trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: A common mistake: The 44th Amendment did NOT abolish the right to property entirely. It shifted it from a 'Fundamental Right' (Part III) to a 'Legal/Constitutional Right' under Article 300A.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: The 42nd Amendment was in 1976 (4+2=6). The 44th Amendment was in 1978 (4+4=8).

exam_strategy_tips: Identify the 'Mini-Constitution' as the 42nd Amendment. This is a recurring direct question in SSC and Railway exams.
Memorize the three words added to the Preamble: Socialist, Secular, Integrity. Note that they were added by the 42nd, not the original constitution.
